evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.118: aut bibat, inquit, aut abeat
Publ. N 64: Nīl nōn aut lēnit aut domat diūturnitās.
terms.comment: One or the other, not both.

evidence: Gell. 1.15.10: vel utī taceat vel utī loquātur
terms.comment: The choice is free, and both may hold.

phrases.english: “let him either drink,” he says, “or go”

phrases.latin: aut librīs mē dēlectō … aut flūctūs numerō
phrases.english: either I enjoy my books or I count the waves

phrases.latin: Nīl nōn aut lēnit aut domat diūturnitās.
phrases.english: There is nothing that time does not either soften or tame.

phrases.latin: frustō … pānis condūcī potest, vel utī taceat vel utī loquātur
phrases.english: he can be hired for a crust of bread, either to keep quiet or to talk
